quiz.q: Under the natural rights philosophy recognized in the Constitution, how does the state relate to fundamental rights?
options: The state grants rights to individuals while retaining sovereign authority to withdraw them at will.
The state merely confirms pre-existing natural rights rather than conferring them upon the individual.
The state invents rights through ordinary legislation solely to enlarge the sphere of state sovereignty.
The state denies natural rights until judicial review creates them through liberal interpretation.
quiz.why: Fundamental rights are rooted in natural rights philosophy, meaning the state confirms rather than confers them, thereby limiting arbitrary state sovereignty.

quiz.q: What was the constitutional significance of inserting Article 31C via the Twenty-fifth Amendment in 1971?
options: It protected laws implementing Articles 39(b) and 39(c) from judicial challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
It placed all Directive Principles beyond the reach of judicial review across all constitutional articles.
It empowered state legislatures to determine criminal penalties for offences created under Part III.
It repealed the Ninth Schedule and eliminated all constitutional immunities for property acquisition laws.
quiz.why: Article 31C shielded laws giving effect to directive principles in Article 39(b) and 39(c) from being invalidated under Articles 14, 19, or 31.

quiz.q: How does the judiciary apply the doctrine of severability when adjudicating unconstitutional provisions in a statute?
options: It strikes down the entire statute immediately whenever any single subsection violates fundamental rights.
It suspends the enforcement of the entire statute until Parliament amends the offending sections.
It strikes down only the unconstitutional provisions while preserving the remaining valid portions of the law.
It overrules the invalid clauses prospectively while leaving past administrative actions completely unaffected.
quiz.why: Under the doctrine of severability, the entire law is not declared invalid; only the unconstitutional portions are severed and struck down.

quiz.q: In the context of Indian judicial review, how does procedural due process differ from substantive due process?
options: Procedural due process applies strictly to civil suits, whereas substantive due process governs criminal prosecutions.
Procedural due process questions legislative wisdom, whereas substantive due process examines bureaucratic administrative delay.
Procedural due process allows citizens to waive fundamental rights, whereas substantive due process bars waiver.
Procedural due process questions executive action, whereas substantive due process questions the wisdom of the law.
quiz.why: Procedural due process scrutinizes executive action and procedure, such as delay in deciding mercy petitions, while substantive due process assesses the fairness and wisdom of the legislation.
